Anfield Stadium stands as one of the most culturally significant structures in world sport. Rather than abandoning its historical foundations for a modern suburban arena, Liverpool F.C. chose a path of architectural evolution, weaving the club's 19th-century soul into a 21st-century sporting fortress.  
Architectural Architecture & Dimensions
Built & Opened: 1884  
Original Construction Cost: Funded initially via private land leases under John Orrell; recent modern standalone stand expansions exceeded £231 million collectively.
Original Architect: Uncredited local builders (1884); iconic early additions engineered by the legendary stadium architect Archibald Leitch (1906 Spion Kop).  
Modern Expansion Designers: KSS Group (Main Stand, 2016).  
Current Seating Capacity: 61,276  
Pitch Surface: Desso GrassMaster hybrid turf (polypropylene fibers interwoven with natural grass).
Field Dimensions: 101 by 68 meters (110.5 yd × 74.4 yd).  
Location: Anfield Road, Liverpool, Merseyside, England, L4 0TH.  
The Four Stands
The Spion Kop: A towering single-tier structure holding 12,390 passionate supporters. Named after the battle ridge of Spion Kop in South Africa, it stands as a unified wall of red.  
The Main Stand: One of the largest single all-seater stands in European football, expanded in 2016 to hold 20,500 people across three tiers. It features a massive cantilevered roof ensuring completely unobstructed sightlines.  
Sir Kenny Dalglish Stand: Originally known as the Kemlyn Road Stand, this two-tier structure houses executive suites and accommodates over 11,000 fans.  
Anfield Road End: Positioned opposite the Kop, its multi-tiered architecture was completely redeveloped between 2021 and 2024 to finalize the stadium's push past the 61,000 capacity threshold.  
Major Events & Historical Records
Record Attendance: 61,905 spectators on February 2, 1952, during an FA Cup 4th-round tie against Wolverhampton Wanderers.  
International Tournaments: Hosted four matches during UEFA Euro 1996 (three group games and a quarter-final).  
Other Major Events: Trans-Atlantic Rugby League matches, boxing championships, and historic music concerts featuring local and international icons.
The Fortress Factor: Liverpool remained completely unbeaten at home in the league across 11 different individual seasons, including structural stretches where opponents went years without winning a domestic fixture on Anfield's turf.  
3 Surprising Lesser-Known Facts
The Blue Origins: Anfield was not built for Liverpool F.C. It opened in 1884 as the home ground of their cross-town rivals, Everton F.C. 1906: Architect Archibald Leitch completes a new bank of terracing along Walton Breck Road, officially named the "Spion Kop" to honor soldiers lost in the Boer War.

1982: The iconic Shankly Gates are erected along Anfield Road, featuring the club's eternal anthem lyrics, "You'll Never Walk Alone".

    -- 4. Compose the UI overlay (dynamic based on district data)

        Title(district.name, position=TopLeft),
        Legend(district.landmarks, position=LeftSide),
        NavigationArrows(position=Bottom),
        LevelIndicator(position=BottomRight)
    ]
in
finalImage
